transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
In its latest employment reports, the Labor Department says only 29,000 jobs were created
last month.
That is far fewer than was expected.
Cornell University students gathered last night in Ithaca, New York.
They're outraged at what many say was the mishandling of a rape case in 2024.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed a special prosecutor to investigate, and PR's
Brian Mann has more.
Hochul says she lost confidence in the local DA, Matthew Van Houten, so Attorney General
Letitia James will take over the probe.
At a gathering last night, Cornell's senior Victoria Campos said students are angry at
the local DA, at their university, and at campus police for their treatment of the alleged
victim, a former student.
I was thinking about her last night before bed.
I am just sending her a lot of support.
I can't imagine how difficult it is.
Local authorities dropped the woman's case two years ago, despite her statement to campus
police that she was raped.
She said in a civil lawsuit filed last month that she was drugged and raped by seven male
students.
Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
The U.S. Postal Service says it'll take extra steps to make sure mail-in ballots for the
midterm elections are delivered on time, and PR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
When there's a federal general election, the U.S. Postal Service rolls out what it calls
"extraordinary measures" for mail-in ballots. For this year's midterms, USPS says it plans
to speed up delivery of ballots beginning a week before Election Day.
And starting October 24, some post offices may extend their opening and closing times
by half-hour, and set up lines or drive-through lanes just for voters who want to get a free
manual postmark for their mail-in ballot.
This plan comes weeks after the Supreme Court blocked the Trump administration from using
USPS to carry out mail-in voting restrictions for the midterms.
Many voting rights advocates are still concerned about last-minute voters getting their ballots
rejected because of late postmarks.
To make sure your ballot gets a postmark on the same day you mail it, USPS recommends
going to a post office and asking for one.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Saudi Arabia says it has handed over the co-pilot of a fly Dubai passenger jet to the United
Arab Emirates.
The pilot of the plane says the co-pilot stabbed him and tried to crash the jet before he was
overpowered by passengers.
The Israeli government says the co-pilot was radicalized.
Philip Mudd served in the CIA and FBI.
He says people want to know what motivated the incident this week.
But investigators are trying to find out if there is any other danger.
The public wants to know why, what just happened, and the investigators want to know whether
there's another who.
That is, the first question an investigator has might not be motivation.
Did anybody know?
Did anybody else participate?
Are there people in a chat room, for example, who might do the same thing?
Mitigating threat is the first question, not figuring out motive.
So they're working on mitigating threat.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
This is NPR.
Lawyers for the condemned woman whom Tennessee failed to execute on Wednesday night say she
is now getting life-saving treatment in a hospital where she is in critical condition.
Krista Pike was supposed to be put to death for murdering classmate Colleen Slemmer in
1995.
Executioners gave Pike two separate lethal injections, but both failed.
Twenty-one states are suing the Trump administration over its repeal of pollution rules involving
power plants across the U.S.
NPR's Julia Simon says the Biden-era rule were meant to reduce emissions from the burning
of fossil fuels.
The 21 states and four cities argue their appeal "guts one of the country's most significant
climate protections" and will worsen the climate crisis.
The Biden-era rules would have required coal and new natural gas plants to install pollution
control equipment that would have significantly reduced carbon dioxide emissions.
When the EPA announced the rule changed last month, they said in their announcement that
greenhouse gas emissions from power plants "have no material impact on climate change."
That is false.
And pollution from power plants also impacts human health.
The EPA says it doesn't comment on ongoing litigation.
Julia Simon, NPR News.
A record increase in electricity rates has gone into effect in Puerto Rico.
Many consumers will see their monthly bills rise about 18 percent.
The Puerto Rican utility says that's due to the war in Iran and higher energy costs.
It's also driven by climate change and hotter summer temperatures.
This is NPR.
